decisions.text: Q3 operating budget is held flat at $2.4M, same as Q2; teams make trade-offs inside it.
Hire two backend engineers in Q3; the data analyst role moves to Q4.
Do not renew Pingwell; move SMS to Brightline Messaging on a one-year contract at 0.6 cents per message.
Outlook two-way sync is the top Q3 priority, group booking second (in parallel); mobile redesign is out of Q3.
Team plan price rises from $12 to $15 per seat per month for new customers, effective September 1.
Existing Team customers keep the $12 price until March 31 next year, then move to $15 with notice.
The annual-plan discount (two months free) stays unchanged this quarter.
Every Sev1 gets a legal-reviewed, customer-facing postmortem within five business days.
All 231 accounts affected by the June 2 reminder incident get a 10% credit on their June invoice.
OpsWorld is back on with a small kiosk instead of the full booth, capped at $18K all in.

actions.task: Send the revised Q3 budget sheet with the flat number and team envelopes.
Pull the AWS cost breakdown by service and environment to explain the 11% cloud increase.
Rewrite the job descriptions for the two backend roles (platform and integrations).
Get the two backend reqs approved with Elena in people ops, copying Speaker 1.
Send Pingwell the non-renewal notice once the Brightline contract is signed.
Send the Brightline contract draft to Priya in legal, flagging the data processing addendum.
Write the SMS cutover migration plan (dual-send ramp, short code port as the long pole).
Pull the list of accounts blocked on Outlook sync with ARR and stage, including ones lost to Agendo.
Update the pricing model with the $15 price and the 2% and 4% churn cases.
Draft the customer email announcing the price change plus a support FAQ.
Ship the dedupe (idempotency) fix for reminder retries.
Apply the 10% incident credits in billing before the July invoice run.
Email the affected accounts about the credit (and call Castellan).
Confirm and book the smaller OpsWorld kiosk with Daniel in marketing.
Take the Brightline call to negotiate a volume tier above 5M messages a month (reassigned from Speaker 1).

traps.text: Using Bluepeak Staffing contractors (about four for six months) instead of full-time hires was proposed and rejected.
The AI rescheduling assistant was left open (not in, not out of Q3); no decision was made.
The early agreement to drop the OpsWorld booth entirely was reversed in wrap-up; it must not appear as a decision.
The Brightline volume-tier negotiation call was first taken by Speaker 1 and later reassigned to You; it must not be listed under Speaker 1.
Keeping Pingwell as a month-to-month fallback if Brightline delivery drops below 98% was only a what-if, not an action.
